character.lede: A two-tone brick family house stands on a riverside lot, with three gables across the front and a glazed entry. A two-car garage, a pond and a picnic table sit around it.

spots.line: A record player, two wingback chairs and a toy box share the family room.
A crib, a glider and a changing table fill the upstairs nursery.
An exercise bike, a bench and a workbench share the garage.

facts.style: Two-storey two-tone brick family traditional on a riverside lot: one long side-gabled ridge with a single dormer, three wall gables across the front (brick over the garage, a tall brick centre gable, a whitewashed gable over a recessed glazed entry), a pent roof over the garage, a bay under its own hip, a lower hipped east wing with the hearth chimney; a rock-edged stream and topiary cones in front, a lily pond and willow on the west lawn, the river behind

character.truths: The Core sits on a credenza in the Family Room, in sight of the door. There is no television and no kitchen island. Riverside lot with ponds, a picnic table and a barbecue. Three generations live here; the baby sleeps in the upstairs nursery.

details.rule: every beat of an adult or teen persona (13 or older) gets a detail (before, after, steps, fact); pair beats first

homehub: No passwords: a "Select your user" box offers every name including Administrator (anyone on the network can pick one)
Extras bundled: recipes, expiry tracker, link shortener, PDF compressor, QR generator
immich: [note] Bundles its own database and a machine-learning service, so first start takes a while.
[note] No API is mentioned in the listing; treat as web interface only for agent purposes.
navidrome: Description says "from anywhere" and "works offline-first": paraphrase, remote access is not claimed
Already in 11 of 30 stories: one short of the cap of 12; rotate music beats to mStream, Swing Music and Music Assistant
project-nomad: [public-access] Ships without authentication. For trusted home networks only. Never describe it as exposed.
[note] amd64 only (fine on the Core). Internet is needed once for setup and downloads.
[claims] Educational content comes from third-party sources. Do not promise grades.
Ships without authentication: home network only, never described as exposed.
Needs the internet once for setup and downloads; never "fully offline" or "anywhere".
excalidraw: [note] amd64 only. An Excalidraw MCP entry exists for agents.
marketplace: Manifest source points to ozencb/excalidraw-persist, a 105-star wrapper, not excalidraw/excalidraw.
home-assistant: [hardware] The Hub package runs without privileged host mounts. Integrations that need direct USB, Bluetooth or D-Bus access (a Zigbee stick, for example) are not enabled by default.
[note] Ships with a Matter server container alongside. Its manifest sets host_access true because that container uses host networking; no USB, Bluetooth or D-Bus access is granted.
[claims] Do not promise energy savings. Home Assistant has no energy figures in the listing.
Matter container uses host networking (host_access true); no USB, Bluetooth or D-Bus access is granted, so no Zigbee stick.
The QA capture is the onboarding page (shows the product, no data).
ci-planning: [cloud-link] Two-way Google Calendar sync exists but is off by default and needs a Google OAuth client. Do not say it never touches Google.
[note] Local-model briefings, task extraction and auto-scheduling appear only when Ollama is reachable.
[note] No API is mentioned in the listing; treat as web interface only for agent purposes.

[cloud-link] Crash reports go to Companion Intelligence unless "Share crash reports" is turned off at install (it is on by default). Credentials, file paths, request bodies and memories are stripped first. Do not write t
Two way Google Calendar sync exists, off by default: never say it never touches Google.
gitea: [note] Gitea Mirror is a different listing (it copies GitHub repositories into Gitea). Name only Gitea. Forgejo does the same job; name one Git host per household.
[note] The listing mentions Actions CI. The package ships the forge and its database only, no runner, so do not show a CI run.
[claims] Say where the repositories are (on the Core). Do not say it syncs with, or is compatible with, GitHub.
Listing mentions Actions CI; no runner ships: never show a CI run.
Gitea Mirror is a different app.
frigate: [hardware] Needs IP cameras that stream over RTSP. Cameras are not part of the Core.
[public-access] Watching cameras from away from home is remote access, which the sheet leaves unfinished.
[claims] No detection-speed or accuracy numbers. Do not say it prevents anything.
QA screenshot shows "No frames have been received, check error logs": reject. The store listing image shows a real backyard photo that is not a Hub capture.
Watching away from home is remote access: not claimed.
mealie: [note] Pasting a recipe URL fetches that web page. Everything it saves stays on your Core.
[qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
pasting a URL fetches that web page
booklore: [cloud-link] Fetches metadata and covers from outside.
audiomass: The Core only serves the page: decoded audio and edits live in the viewer's browser, so "sits on the Core" is false until the person saves a file where they choose
Short description says "audio never leaves the appliance": an absolute; paraphrase
opencode: [cloud-link] The Hub wires it to the Core's local model by default (hub_integration inference). The app can also connect to cloud providers with a key you add inside it; leave that off. A coding agent is private only on
[claims] Never claim parity with a hosted coding model and never a speed figure. The agent edits files, so the beat shows the person approving the change (agents prepare, people approve).
[note] The web interface has no sign-in unless a server password is set at install. The older OpenCode Web listing is superseded; name only OpenCode.
[note] Added 2026-10-15 for the builder archetype: the old cloud-or-developer exclusion lumped it with apps that need cloud keys; this one is wired to the local model.
[qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
ollama: [note] The Hub also has its own built-in Ollama service. Many listings say "the Hub built-in Ollama".
[claims] Model sizes and speeds come only from the fact sheet table. No own tok/s.

[claims] This package serves on the CPU unless the host passes a GPU in (not enabled by default), so say nothing about speed. It has no chat window of its own: it sits behind Open WebUI or an agent. It asks for no cloud
[qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
No chat UI of its own: sits behind Open WebUI or an agent.
it-tools: Listing says it keeps working with the network unplugged: do not repeat (install and updates use the internet).
Everything computes in the browser; the Core serves static files only.
hoppscotch: Without sign-in, collections stay in the browser, not on the Core
Heavy for a client tool: three containers
blockbench: Projects live in the browser (IndexedDB) or in files the person saves: the Core serves the app, it does not hold the models
The listing names Minecraft models; say "game models" or "block models" in copy
Free-text store claim "never sees your models" is accurate for the container
habitica: The sign-up page in the capture carries a cookie-consent banner: check the self-hosted build for analytics scripts before saying it sends nothing out
Game, not a health or behaviour tool: no outcomes
calibre-web: [qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
marketplace: Documented default admin credentials (admin / admin123); no QA capture.
homebox: [note] Barcode and Open Food Facts lookups call outside services.
[qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
Analytics are switched off in the manifest (good)
yamtrack: [cloud-link] Imports from Trakt, MyAnimeList and TMDB are outside services.
Lists and ratings only: no health or behaviour claims
